answers.question: Should a new repair job be created?
answers.answer: No. R-4801 is open for the same tap with a confirmed visit; a new job would duplicate it. The worsening is a routine drip, not a flood.

answers.question: What do you reply to the tenant?
answers.answer: Said the existing job covers it, gave the 15 Oct 08:00-12:00 visit, said we'd ask for an earlier slot without promising one, and gave isolation-valve advice.

answers.question: What, if anything, do you change on existing records?
answers.answer: Added note NOTE-101 to R-4801 recording the worsening; no stage, contractor or visit changes.

args.body: Hi Amelia, thanks for letting us know. We already have a job open for your kitchen tap (R-4801), so we haven't opened a new one. Swift Plumbing & Heating are booked for Thursday 15 October, 08:00-12:00. We've added a note that the drip is getting worse and will ask them whether they can come sooner; I can't promise that yet. In the meantime, you can turn the small isolation valve under the sink (a slot you turn a quarter turn with a screwdriver) to stop the water to the tap, and put a bowl under it. If water starts leaking elsewhere or you can't stop it, please call us straight away.
